title: Linear Equations
subtitle: Both Sides, Solution Count & Systems
bounds: PROTOCOL 4a and 4b (coordinates and lines), grade 8. One variable letter per equation, written ax + b = cx + d or with one group p(x + t); every coefficient of size 1-10 (p 2-6). Constants: when any literal is negative, every constant (and every distributed product p times t) has size at most 12, otherwise at most 20. After collecting terms the x coefficient has size 2-10 and the number side is the times-table product of it and the solution (size at most 100). Solutions are integers of size 1-10, never 0 (x = 0 is only ever a distractor); T3 counts are one, none or infinite, and the one-solution equations also have a nonzero integer solution of size at most 10. T4: fractions 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5 written (1/k)x or x/k and decimals 0.5, 0.25, 0.2, 0.1, every x a times-table multiple so the solution is an integer of size at most 40 and the collected number side is a whole number of size at most 10; both-sided coefficient pairs (1, 1/2), (1/2, 1/4), (0.5, 1), (0.5, 0.25). T5: lines y = mx + b with m of size 1-6 and b of size at most 12; sum-or-difference systems have coefficients 1-2, an integer solution of size 1-8 with x not equal to y, constants of size at most 20 (at most 12 if one is negative), solved by adding the two equations only; crossing lines meet at integer coordinates of size at most 10.

tiers.name: Both Sides
tiers.description: x on both sides: collect the x terms, then the numbers.

tiers.name: Distribute, Solve
tiers.description: Distribute first, then solve with x on both sides.

tiers.name: One, None, Infinite
tiers.description: Decide how many solutions an equation has.

tiers.name: Systems
tiers.description: Two lines at once: how many points, and where.

SAME_SIGN_MOVE.student: To move 3x across the = sign, subtract 3x from both sides. Don't add it.
SAME_SIGN_MOVE.teacher: Moves a variable term across the equals sign without changing its sign: 5x + 2 = 3x + 10 becomes 8x = 8.

CONST_SIGN.student: Undo + 2 by subtracting 2 from both sides. Undo − 2 by adding 2.
CONST_SIGN.teacher: Moves a constant across the equals sign without changing its sign (adds instead of subtracts).

ONE_STEP.student: Stopped early: 2x = 8 still has to be divided by 2.
ONE_STEP.teacher: Stops at the collected equation (ax = k) and reports k as the answer.

SIGN_SLIP.student: Right size, wrong sign. Put your x back in to check.
SIGN_SLIP.teacher: Subtracts the x terms the wrong way round and answers with the opposite sign.

PARTIAL_DIST.student: Multiply the outside number by EVERY term inside: 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6.
PARTIAL_DIST.teacher: Distributes only to the variable: 3(x + 2) becomes 3x + 2.

SIGN_INSIDE.student: 3(x − 2) = 3x − 6. The minus sign stays with the 2.
SIGN_INSIDE.teacher: Loses the negative inside the parentheses when distributing: 3(x − 2) becomes 3x + 6.

DROP_LIKE_TERM.student: Don't lose the extra x. Count every x term after distributing.
DROP_LIKE_TERM.teacher: Drops the loose x term when collecting like terms after distributing.

CANCEL_IS_ZERO.student: When the x terms cancel, there is no x left to be 0. Look at the numbers.
CANCEL_IS_ZERO.teacher: Reads an equation whose variable terms cancel as x = 0.

ALWAYS_ONE.student: Not every equation has one answer. If the x terms cancel, check the numbers.
ALWAYS_ONE.teacher: Assumes every linear equation has exactly one solution.

NONE_FOR_IDENTITY.student: If both sides come out equal (6 = 6), it is true for EVERY x.
NONE_FOR_IDENTITY.teacher: Reads a true statement with no variable left (an identity) as no solution.

INFINITE_FOR_FALSE.student: If the x terms cancel and the numbers differ (4 = 7), it is never true.
INFINITE_FOR_FALSE.teacher: Reads a false statement with no variable left (a contradiction) as infinitely many solutions.

ONE_IS_MANY.student: x on both sides does not mean many answers. Collect x and get one value.
ONE_IS_MANY.teacher: Believes variables on both sides produce infinitely many solutions.

ONE_IS_NONE.student: x on both sides can still be solved: collect the x terms and divide.
ONE_IS_NONE.teacher: Believes variables on both sides mean the equation cannot be solved.

ZERO_GUESS.student: Try x = 0 in the equation: the sides don't match. Solve it instead.
ZERO_GUESS.teacher: Guesses x = 0 instead of counting solutions.

CONST_FOR_COEFF.student: Match like with like: x terms with x terms, numbers with numbers.
CONST_FOR_COEFF.teacher: Puts a constant where the coefficient belongs (or the reverse) when matching two sides.

SIGN_PICK.student: Right size, wrong sign. The two sides must match exactly, sign included.
SIGN_PICK.teacher: Matches the size of the number on the other side but flips its sign.

DIVIDE_FOR_MULT.student: (1/2)x = 4 means x is 2 times bigger: multiply by 2, don't divide.
DIVIDE_FOR_MULT.teacher: Divides by the denominator to undo a fractional coefficient instead of multiplying.

FORGOT_LAST_STEP.student: Stopped early: you still have to undo the fraction or decimal on x.
FORGOT_LAST_STEP.teacher: Stops at the collected equation and answers with the number side.

ONE_TERM_CLEARED.student: To clear a fraction, multiply EVERY term on both sides, not just one.
ONE_TERM_CLEARED.teacher: Multiplies only the fractional term (or one side) by the denominator.

DEC_WRONG_WAY.student: 0.5x = 3 means x is 2 times bigger. Divide by 0.5, which doubles.
DEC_WRONG_WAY.teacher: Multiplies by the decimal coefficient instead of dividing by it.

DEC_AS_FRAC.student: 0.5 is 1/2, not 1/5. Read a decimal as a part of one whole.
DEC_AS_FRAC.teacher: Reads the digit after the decimal point as the denominator: 0.5 as 1/5.

PARALLEL_ONE.student: Same slope, different start: parallel lines never meet.
PARALLEL_ONE.teacher: Thinks two lines with the same slope still cross once.

SAME_SLOPE_SAME_LINE.student: Same slope but different starts are different lines. They never touch.
SAME_SLOPE_SAME_LINE.teacher: Reads two parallel lines as the same line, with infinitely many shared points.

TWO_LINES_TWO.student: A solution is a point on BOTH lines. Two lines don't mean two solutions.

STOPPED_AT_SUM.student: After adding the equations, divide: 3x = 15 means x = 5.
STOPPED_AT_SUM.teacher: Reports the added constants without dividing by the combined coefficient.

GAVE_OTHER.student: Check which variable the question asks for.
GAVE_OTHER.teacher: Solves correctly but reports the other variable.

SWAPPED_XY.student: Points are written (x, y): x first, then y.
SWAPPED_XY.teacher: Reverses the coordinates of the solution point.

READ_CONSTANT.student: x − y = 4 does not say y is 4. Solve for both variables.
READ_CONSTANT.teacher: Reads a constant from an equation as the value of a variable.

INTERCEPT_AS_MEET.student: The y-intercept is where a line crosses the y-axis, not where the lines meet.
INTERCEPT_AS_MEET.teacher: Gives the y-intercept of a line as the intersection point.

DROPPED_SLOPE.student: Put x into the WHOLE rule: y = 3x + 4 uses 3 times x.
DROPPED_SLOPE.teacher: Finds y by substituting x without the slope multiplier.

items.explanation: Infinite needs identical sides, so the x terms match: k = 8.

items.prompt: y = −6x − 1 and y = −6x + 6. How many solutions?
items.explanation: Both lines have slope −6 but start at −1 and 6: parallel, no shared point.

items.prompt: x + y = 10 and x − y = −6. Find y.
items.explanation: Add the equations: 2x = 4, so x = 2. Put it back: y = 8.

items.prompt: y = 5x + 4 and y = −x + 10. Where do they meet?
items.explanation: Set equal: 5x + 4 = −x + 10, so x = 1. Then y = 9.

items.prompt: x + y = 9 and y − x = −1. Find x.
items.explanation: Add the equations: 2y = 8, so y = 4. Put it back: x = 5.

items.prompt: y = 6x + 10 and y − 6x = −1. How many solutions?
items.explanation: Both lines have slope 6 but start at 10 and −1: parallel, no shared point.
